All the work you didn't go to law school to do, now handled by AI agents.

rows.body:
Meta is the best channel for law firms to sign new clients right now. Most firms just run it wrong.

Three things separate the firms printing cases from the ones burning budget:

1. Intake — are you calling and texting the lead inside 1–5 minutes, or the next morning?

2. Creative — vertical video, 60 seconds or less, in real volume. Not two polished videos a year.

3. Data quality — tracking the lead past the form fill, back to a signed case, and feeding that into Meta.

Get all three right and Facebook starts hunting for the people who actually sign.

Book a call — we'll audit your setup free.

The window is closing for personal injury law firms nationwide.

With new laws like California's SB37 and Colorado's SB26-174 taking effect in 2026, regulators are officially targeting lead-generation models that rely on selling client contact information. Other states are already evaluating similar legislation, and many industry experts expect additional restrictions to follow.

These regulations carry significant civil and criminal penalties for paying third parties for prospective client contact details.

The rest of the country will soon follow suit.

Stop relying on third-party leads that don't represent your integrity and start building a brand that can survive the upcoming legal shifts.

If you want to generate cases through Meta the same way major lead sellers do, while building an asset you actually own, book a call with our team.

Criminal defense lawyers are massively underserved by marketing agencies.

No.

rows.body:
"Ms. Bingaman, do not interrupt me again."

Judge Jared Boyd said that to Patty Bingaman on September 21, 2026, in Union County Circuit Court. Her husband, Russell, had been dead since January 2025. She stood in front of the judge with no lawyer and a binder of accounting, and she asked for one thing: keep Russell's estate open so she could keep going after his records.

The hearing lasted 14 minutes. Thirty-seven minutes after it ended, Judge Boyd signed the judgment Patty had asked him, in writing, not to sign. It came from the lawyer she had fired five weeks earlier.

This is A Marriage on the Record, Part Three: Keep It Open.

Patty knew what the estate meant. "If I give that PR up, I'm just his wife."

Carol Fredrick, her lawyer in McMinnville, told her on a recorded call, "We can hold it open." In July, Carol put it in writing: "This keeps the estate open." Then Patty read paragraph six of the judgment Carol's office wrote for the judge to sign. That sentence isn't in it. On August 16, at 9:38 at night, Patty fired her. "Under paragraph six, I am not asked, and I do not decide."

Then the courtroom. In 14 minutes Judge Boyd said almost 2,000 words. Patty got a little over 300. He cut her off 14 times. At one point he fired five questions at her in 42 seconds. And he's the one who told her to stop interrupting.

He told her probate is "divvying up property, no more, no less, not a mechanism for investigations." In this episode I show you what he signs in other people's estates. In an estate handled by Wyatt Baum, the same lawyer who represented Shawn and Austin Bingaman in Russell's guardianship, the money had already gone out to the family, the estate stayed open, and Judge Boyd approved a $400,000 wrongful death settlement. In an estate handled by Damien Yervasi, Tempie Bartell's lawyer, the only asset was a wrongful death claim, and Judge Boyd signed the order dividing up the settlement. Another estate was held open six years to sue Grande Ronde Hospital, and Judge Boyd signed the judgment that closed it. Patty asked for the same thing. Wyatt Baum's clients got it. Damien Yervasi's clients got it. Patty got a lecture.

He said his name was announced at the start of the hearing. The court's own recording says it never was. That afternoon he put it in a signed order anyway, and a few lines later he wrote, "It is unclear whether this is due to limited capacity or just simple stubbornness."

Judge Boyd sat on the board of the Mount Emily Safe Center. His wife, Jill, chaired it. Tempie Bartell, who ran Nadine's Nest, where Russell lived, was its medical director for more than 20 years. I believe this is Judge Boyd protecting Tempie Bartell again, first in the guardianship, now in Russell's estate.

Here's what Judge Boyd and Carol Fredrick didn't count on: paragraph six. That judgment doesn't close the estate. It closes when receipts are filed, and Patty won't file them. The estate is still open. Patty is still Russell's personal representative.

As Patty said while Russell was still alive: "This old gal ain't giving up."

Part Four, Awake, comes out next weekend.

Start from the beginning with Part One, The Locked Door: https://youtu.be/1qgA08TEPeM

I'm Levi Bakke, Valor Investigates.
www.valor-investigations.com

We built a new system that’s helping personal injury, family law, estate planning, immigration, and criminal defense law firms land more signed cases.

And it’s not a generic answering service that routes your callers through anonymous agents…

Or a clunky bot that people hang up on. 

Because if we’re being honest… 

Every answering service, every front desk, and every bot does the same thing.

They answer, take a message, and email it to you. 

And that’s where the call dies while the caller hires whoever answers first. 

Which is why this new system turns every caller into a contact your firm owns and can continue following up with…

So you can turn more of the leads you're already generating into signed cases.

All by responding immediately... 

Following up automatically until they book or sign…

And reactivating the dead leads already in your database.

Without you lifting a finger in as little as 14 days.

And the best part is…

It’s built 100% done-for-you, and every call is answered... every lead is followed up... or your month is free.

Every single month.

We call it The Signed-Case System, and here’s exactly how it works:

First, we give you a dedicated intake team trained specifically on your firm…

With bilingual English and Spanish receptionists…

So every caller feels like they've reached your office... not another answering service.

Then our 24/7 AI ensures every after-hours call, text, and web lead receives an immediate response…

In both English and Spanish…

So nights, weekends, and after-hours stop becoming free signed cases for your competitors.

Next, we install our Signed-Case Engine…

So every caller becomes a contact your firm owns…

And every lead keeps hearing from your firm until they book, sign, or tell you they're not interested... instead of becoming another dead message buried in your inbox.

And finally, everything plugs into the software you already use, so you can sign more cases without changing how your firm operates.

So, if you want the new system for landing more signed clients this year…

Click this ad.
Fill out a short form.
And book a quick call. 

We’ll walk you through our system…

Show you how it could fill your firm with more signed cases…

And why law firms like yours have trusted us to answer their phones since 2007.

So, click this ad to schedule your call now.
rows.title: For Law Firm Owners

rows.body:
The window is closing for personal injury law firms nationwide.

With new laws like California's SB37 and Colorado's SB26-174 taking effect in 2026, regulators are officially targeting lead-generation models that rely on selling client contact information. Other states are already evaluating similar legislation, and many industry experts expect additional restrictions to follow.

These regulations carry significant civil and criminal penalties for paying third parties for prospective client contact details.

The rest of the country will soon follow suit.

Stop relying on third-party leads that don't represent your integrity and start building a brand that can survive the upcoming legal shifts.

If you want to generate cases through Meta the same way major lead sellers do, while building an asset you actually own, book a call with our team.
